groups.summary: The constructor-kind guard prevents JavaScript function constructors from receiving their allocated this object.
groups.evidence: At intro, js_ts/semantic/syntax.rs:147-153 inventories function Item as ProcedureKind::Function (full prefix crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/). js_ts/semantic/inventory.rs:177-198 and js_ts/semantic/mod.rs:377-383 make a function reading this own a receiver; js_ts/semantic/values.rs:1102-1108 publishes it. js_ts/semantic/control.rs:2468-2469 gives new Item(x) no receiver operand, and :2555-2557 allocates its result. semantic/oracle/call.rs:487-488 now rejects that allocation solely because the target is Function. semantic/workspace_oracle/value_flow.rs:5067-5083 consequently cannot bind the allocated result; its implicit receiver fallback (:1374-1404) cannot supply this from an ordinary caller function. The binding stays open at :5122-5123 with no Receiver transport, losing receiver-based member effects. The base helper in value_flow.rs:1021-1030 matched the result allocation without the new kind restriction, and therefore supplied this actual. No matching later fix was identified.

groups.summary: Reverse-index construction retains all importers' resolved declaration sets simultaneously outside the memo-cache budget.
groups.evidence: At intro, src/analyzer/capabilities.rs:71-74 collects every resolved BTreeSet<CodeUnit> before the reduction at :76-86. Go resolution at src/analyzer/go_analyzer.rs:199-215 includes all non-module declarations of matching package files; JavaScript wildcard resolution at src/analyzer/javascript_analyzer.rs:175-181 does likewise. For N files importing one package/module with D declarations, the vector retains N*D CodeUnits even though the reverse map needs only file edges. CodeUnit owns cloned String fields (src/analyzer/model.rs:162-169). Cache hits also return cloned sets (go_analyzer.rs:185-187; javascript_analyzer.rs:165-167), so cache eviction cannot release the vector's copies. The old helper (capabilities.rs:49-60) consumed one candidate set at a time. This introduces an unbounded temporary working set capable of exhausting memory on large repositories. Later commit 2111bf7a3d8407be937879be8250e4034d504014 removes the all-CodeUnit-sets vector by projecting to file edges inside the parallel closure; it still retains a temporary edge vector and is not proof of fully bounded memory.

groups.summary: The claimed newly quadratic Go cold lookup already occurred through the old filter's full-resolution fallback.
groups.evidence: At intro, src/analyzer/go_analyzer.rs:270-287 shows could_import_file falling back to imported_code_units_of(source_file) whenever the requested target does not match an import path. This fallback is unchanged from base 5cfbe06f0104331f1899b2a8a666865eb432d62f, go_analyzer.rs:259-276. The old referencing_files_via_imports helper (src/analyzer/capabilities.rs:49-59) called that predicate for every candidate, then resolved matching candidates too. Thus nonmatching importers were not cheaply filtered out: a cold lookup already reached the all_files scan (intro go_analyzer.rs:190-207) for essentially every candidate. The new eager index does not introduce the claimed asymptotic regression.

groups.summary: JavaScript's higher first-lookup work is the explicit tradeoff of the reusable whole-project reverse index.
groups.evidence: At intro, src/analyzer/javascript_analyzer.rs:226-234 intentionally builds a OnceLock-backed reverse index from every analyzed file, so it does perform more forward resolution on a sparse first query than the old capabilities.rs:53-59 filter using javascript_analyzer.rs:266-276. However, subsequent distinct target queries reuse that index instead of repeating a repository scan. The intro commit message explicitly identifies replacing on-demand per-target scans with one cached project-wide index as the change's purpose. The finding supplies no measured timeout, violated latency contract, or independent correctness failure beyond this intentional cold-versus-repeated-query tradeoff; the separate excessive temporary declaration retention is covered by g1. Later 04f4b4c7aee69455df5c32563ee1a03b30021a9c deliberately extends the same shared lazy indexing design to Java and Python.
